key_terms.meaning: Slab supported on two opposite edges and designed as a 1 m wide beam spanning the short direction.
Slab with long span less than twice short span, carrying load in both directions.
Continuous or discontinuous support edge that decides the IS 456 moment coefficient.
Slab fixed at one edge only, producing hogging moment at the support.
Slab on three or more supports, designed with code coefficients that allow for pattern loading.
Loading alternate spans to obtain the largest positive and negative design moments.
Two flights between floors with a half-space landing, reversing direction at the landing.
Inclined slab in a staircase that carries the steps and acts as a one-way slab between landings.
Horizontal distance between two consecutive risers along a flight.
Vertical height of one step, from top of one tread to top of the next.
Horizontal top surface of a step where the foot rests.
Design span used in moment and deflection calculations, taken as clear span plus effective depth or centre-to-centre support, as code permits.
Factor √(R² + T²)/T that converts waist-slab load per horizontal metre to load along the inclined slab; R is riser and T is tread.
Stair with a central opening or well, flights arranged around it.
Slab supported directly on columns, usually with drop panels or column capitals, without beams.
Strip of a flat slab on each side of the column centreline, carrying the larger part of the moment.
Flat-slab strip between column strips, carrying the remaining moment.
Line of plastic hinges in a slab at collapse, across which reinforcement yields.
Energy method that equates work done by loads to work absorbed at yield lines.
Load at which a slab forms a mechanism and can deflect without further load increase.

takeaways: One-way slabs are designed as 1 m wide beams in the short span; two-way slabs need coefficients in both directions when long span is less than twice short span.
Cantilever slabs have fixed-end hogging moment, while continuous slabs use code coefficients that already include pattern-loading effects.
In a dog-legged staircase the inclined waist slab behaves as a one-way slab between landings, with slope factor converting vertical loads to inclined-slab loads.
Open well, stringer beam and cantilever tread stairs suit different plan constraints and change the load path.
Flat slabs send load directly to columns; total static moment splits into negative and positive parts and then into column and middle strips.
Yield line theory uses assumed hinge lines and virtual work, and its collapse load is an upper bound on the true collapse load.
Detailing, deflection and shear checks often govern slab thickness as much as flexural steel does.

glossary.def: Flat plate member carrying transverse load mainly by bending.
Slab that bends only in one direction and is designed as a 1 m wide beam.
Slab that bends in two directions because long span is less than twice short span.
Ratio of long span to short span of a slab panel.
Support condition that decides whether an edge is continuous or discontinuous for coefficient selection.
Distance from extreme compression fibre to centroid of tension reinforcement.
Distance between inner faces of supports.
Design span used in calculations, based on clear span and support conditions.
Member fixed at one end and free at the other.
Bending moment that causes tension at the top of a slab or beam.
Bending moment that causes tension at the bottom of a slab or beam.
Slab running over three or more supports, with continuity reducing positive moments.
Arrangement of live load on selected spans to produce critical design moments.
Stair with two flights and a half-space landing between floors.
Inclined slab forming the structural spine of a staircase flight.
Vertical height of one step.
Horizontal top surface of one step.
Horizontal distance between successive risers.
Level platform between flights or at floor level.
Slab supported directly by columns without beams.
Flat-slab strip beside the column centreline that carries a major share of moment.
Flat-slab strip between column strips.
Line of plastic hinging in a slab at collapse.
Energy balance between external load work and internal work at yield lines.
Load at which a slab mechanism forms.
Collapse load from an assumed mechanism that is not lower than the true collapse load.
